Famille noyée à Akwesasne – Deux ans apr: Family Drowned in Akwesasne – Two Years Later, Relatives Face an Asylum System That Fails the Roma
Deux ans après la mort de la famille Ior: Two years after the deaths of the Iordache family, their relatives are now seeking asylum themselves, in a Canadian system biased against the Roma community.
Claudio Rafael et Ana Maria dans leur ap: Claudio Rafael and Ana Maria in the two-bedroom semi-basement apartment where they live with their three children. Photo: Zied Ben Romdhane
J’ai rencontré la famille Firu, des Roms: I met the Firu family, Roma originally from Romania, twice over the past two weeks. The father, Claudio Rafael, wrote to our editor-in-chief, Lela Savić, to tell her he was seeking asylum in Canada for his family and was struggling. Lela had already been in contact with them two years ago, when she wrote about the Iordache couple and their two young children, who tragically lost their lives trying to cross the border between Canada and the United States on March 29, 2023. For the first time, Claudio Rafael, Florin Iordache’s brother, is speaking out.
Lors de la première rencontre, Lela – qu: At our first meeting, Lela – who speaks Romani – came with me to translate what Claudio Rafael couldn’t always express the way he wanted to in French. He told us about his struggle, his still-raw grief and the crushing debts weighing on his family. But this is not only a story of suffering. It is also a story of fighting a system that seems to ignore them and does not always recognize the persecution Roma people endure. A system that seems to consider them not to be asylum seekers like any others.
Lors de ma deuxième rencontre avec la fa: At my second meeting with the family, I was alone. After making calls and doing a great deal of research to understand why the couple still hadn’t received their work permits more than eight months after filing their asylum claim, I decided to step out of my role as a journalist for a moment. I contacted immigration services to find out more about the status of their applications.
J’ai également communiqué avec Izabela T: I also reached out to Izabela Tiberiade, a human rights researcher and activist working for the recognition of the Roma genocide, and Gina Csanyi-Robah, director and founder of the Canadian Romani Alliance. Both describe the systemic barriers facing Roma in Canada, and the need for a new federal policy to welcome them.
L’histoire des Firu n’est pas seulement: The Firus’ story is not only personal; it speaks for all the families living in precarity and exile. Thousands of people, like them, are quietly fighting the same battle, searching for a place that will take them in, a place where it is possible to hope for a better future.
Nous dédions cet article à la mémoire de: We dedicate this article to the memory of the Iordache family, who died on March 29, 2023: Florin, 28, Cristina, 28, their two-year-old daughter Evelin and their one-year-old son Eylin. We also dedicate it to the Indian Chaudhari family, who perished with them in the waters of the St. Lawrence: Praveenbhai, 50, Dakshaben, 45, their son Meet, 20, and their daughter Vidhi, 23.
<strong>La mort des quatre membres d’une: The deaths of four members of a Roma family – a couple and their children – sent a shockwave through the community on March 29, 2023. The Iordaches drowned while trying to cross the border into the United States at Akwesasne, after Canada denied them refugee status and while they faced deportation. Two years later, we meet the brother of Florin Iordache, the late father of the family, who is now seeking asylum himself, in a Canadian system riddled with biases against the Roma community. Our report.
« Depuis ce jour, depuis que j’ai perdu: “Since that day, since I lost my son, my life is over, I died with them,” says Claudio Rafael Firu, who speaks of his younger brother as a “son.” When you dive into the ocean blue of this man’s eyes, a few grey flecks of foam hint at the storm that has been tearing at his soul for two years. On March 29, 2023, the bodies of his brother Florin, 28, his sister-in-law Cristina, 28, their two-year-old daughter Evelin and their one-year-old son Eylin were found in the St. Lawrence River, on Mohawk territory at Akwesasne, near the American border. Four members of the Chaudhari family, from western India, also drowned in the river’s icy waters: Praveenbhai, 50, Dakshaben, 45, their son Meet, 20, and their daughter Vidhi, 23.
Après quatre années passées au Canada, l: After four years in Canada, the birth of two children, two asylum claims, a Pre-Removal Risk Assessment (PRRA) application refused in 2023 and the dismissal of their appeal of that decision, <l1>the Iordache family faced deportation</l1> and were about to be sent back to their country of origin: Romania.
Florin Iordache, 28 ans, Cristina Iordac: Florin Iordache, 28, Cristina Iordache, 28, their daughter Evelin and their son Eylin, both born in Canada and citizens. Photo: courtesy of Peter Ivanyi
Dans la ville de Craiova, où la famille: In the city of Craiova, where the Iordache family lived before going into exile, stands one of the largest Roma neighbourhoods in Europe. For the young couple, it was out of the question to make their children live through the suffering they had endured as Roma in a segregationist, discriminatory Romanian society. Even if it meant risking their lives. “They didn’t know what else to do, they were desperate, and they got in touch with smugglers,” says the eldest of the siblings.
C’est dans un appartement en demi-sous-s: Claudio Rafael and Ana Maria Firu welcome us into a semi-basement apartment where the light barely gets in. Over coffee, they tell us what led them to seek asylum in Canada, despite the tragedy whose scars they still carry. On International Romani Day, this Tuesday, April 8, 2025, La Converse gives them the floor.
<strong>S’endetter pour enterrer les sie: Going into debt to bury their own
Lorsqu’on lui demande de parler de la jo: When asked to talk about the day of March 29, 2023, Claudio Rafael Firu turns toward the window. His gaze drifts, as if he is sinking back into that traumatic memory. “The week before they died, I didn’t speak to my brother at all. He had decided to use a smuggler and I didn’t agree. I told him I had a really bad feeling, that he shouldn’t do it, that I would join him in Canada and we would find another way to cross the border, if need be…” he recalls, tears in his eyes. Florin’s older brother was in Florida at the time. When he was told of their deaths, he was in shock. “I blame myself, it’s my fault, I couldn’t convince him, even though I knew it wasn’t going to go well.”
Les larmes roulent désormais sur les jou: Tears now roll down the cheeks of the man whose life was upended that day. Devastated, Claudio Rafael Firu returned to Romania to prepare the funerals. “We borrowed money from community members to bring the bodies back to our village. It was $21,000 per person, so $84,000 for the four. And that was after negotiating! At first, they were asking $26,000 per body,” he says. Then he had to pay for the cemetery plot.
Claudio Rafael Firu montre des photos du: Claudio Rafael Firu shows photos of the burial vault he chose to bury his brother, his wife and their two children in Romania. Photo: Zied Ben Romhdane.
Comme le veut la tradition romani, les c: As Romani tradition dictates, the bodies were laid out and watched over in the family home before burial. Then, for 40 days, visitors came one after another to offer their condolences and support the grieving family. “The whole village came, then people came from all over Europe. Morning, noon and night, we had to offer food, and bring in musicians, especially since my brother was a well-known musician… All of that costs a lot of money. Hundreds of people came,” says Claudio Rafael Firu.
Cet élan de solidarité a été à la hauteu: This outpouring of solidarity matched the shock felt by the community. But the price of that love is heavy. Between repatriating the bodies, the burial and the reception for the guests, the family racked up more than $100,000 in debt. Fundraisers were organized to help them, but the amounts raised are far from enough.
Claudio Rafael et sa femme restent alors: Claudio Rafael and his wife stayed in Romania to support the family’s matriarch, deeply affected by the loss of her children and grandchildren. They paid down their debts little by little until the day they no longer could, so exorbitant were the monthly payments demanded, part of it interest. Claudio Rafael’s mother was diagnosed with cancer, requiring chemotherapy and costly medical follow-up. To cope with this new blow, the family opened a <l1>GoFundMe campaign</l1> to cover the new expenses. But it remains desperately empty.
Derrière son mari, accoudée à la fenêtre: Behind her husband, leaning on the windowsill, Ana Maria explains: “We tried to sell the house to pay off the debts and leave with whatever money was left. But nobody wanted to buy a house where four people had died. People think it will bring them bad luck,” she says. With no other option, the couple ended up accepting the offer of their main creditor: “He took the house for a very low price, and it paid off part of our debts. Now my mother has to sleep at different people’s homes in the meantime, because she no longer has a place to live,” Claudio Rafael sighs.
<strong>« On ne voulait pas venir au Can: “We didn’t want to come to Canada”
« Je me suis fait deux promesses quand m: “I made myself two promises when my brother died: to take care of our brother who has a disability – whom Florin helped whenever he could by sending money – and to take care of our mother. That’s why we came here: to have a chance to earn a better living and give our children a future,” says the father.
Deux années se sont écoulées, mais il re: Two years have passed, but he remains frozen in a grief that consumes him. He has suffered from insomnia every day since the tragedy. “I’m only 39, and all my hair and my beard have turned white and grey. I’ve lost so much weight that I don’t even recognize myself in the mirror.” He hands us an identity document. With brown hair, a neatly trimmed beard and full cheeks, the man in the photo is indeed someone else.
Claudio Rafael l’admet : au départ, ce n: Claudio Rafael admits it: at first, Canada wasn’t where he wanted to settle his family. Toronto was only supposed to be a stopover on the way to the United States. “I didn’t want to live in the country that pushed my brother and his family toward death by refusing their asylum claim,” he says, running his hand through his hair. Angry at the country he holds responsible for the deaths of his loved ones, he ultimately resolved to claim asylum in Canada for his family, after they missed their connecting flight at Toronto’s airport on April 24, 2024. “As we say back home: nothing happens by chance. It’s our destiny,” he says in a resigned tone.
Aujourd’hui, malgré les dettes suspendue: Today, despite the debts hanging over their heads, the Firu family want to believe in a better future. The couple know the asylum process can take several years, but they are worried about having heard nothing on their work permit applications. Unable to hold a job, the couple can no longer pay their rent and risk eviction.
<strong>« Les demandes de permis de trav: “The work permit applications were in the wrong department”
« Notre loyer, à lui seul, coûte 1 500 $: “Our rent alone is $1,500!” says Ana Maria, handing us the notice she received from their landlord. They haven’t been able to pay it for two months and are waiting for a summons from the housing tribunal. “How do they expect us to pay our rent, feed our children, pay the bills, clothe them for school… with $1,500 and without letting us work?” the mother asks.
Ana Maria pointe un bouquet de roses pla: Ana Maria points to a bunch of roses in a bucket of water near the couch. Their bright colours stand out against the darkness of the apartment. She sells them one by one to try to earn a few dollars. With $1,500 in social assistance, the family of four can no longer make ends meet.
Grâce à l’aide juridique, Claudio Rafael: With legal aid, Claudio Rafael wrote several times to the lawyer handling their case to get news of their work permits. “She says she doesn’t know, and gives us a phone number, but I don’t understand anything. When I call, I can never reach anyone,” he says. He struggles to express himself fluently in French, which complicates his phone communication with immigration services. In the lawyer’s reply emails that we were able to consult, she indeed simply says that she is not in charge of following up on work permits and gives the number for Immigration. Despite several attempts, La Converse was unable to obtain an interview with her.
Face au désarroi de Claudio Rafael, nous: Seeing Claudio Rafael’s distress, we decide to contact Immigration ourselves. “Welcome to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada!” The robotic voice echoes from the cellphone speaker. Very quickly, we are offered different options: “Press 1,” “Press 5”… After three unsuccessful attempts, we finally manage to speak to an Immigration agent. He puts us on hold. A few minutes later, the verdict comes: “the work permit applications were in the wrong department, so nobody processed them.” The couple’s hopeful faces soon give way to incomprehension, then shock.
« Donc là, leur demande n’a pas avancé d: “So their application hasn’t moved forward at all?
– C’est ça. Mais c’est bon, j’ai envoyé: – That’s right. But it’s okay, I sent both applications to the right department this time. So they’ll be able to be processed.
– Quand ? Ce sont des demandeurs d’asile: – When? They’re asylum seekers and they need to work.
– Ce sera moins de 111 jours, mais je ne: – It will be less than 111 days, but I can’t tell you more precisely how long.”
Une heure s’est écoulée lorsque nous rac: An hour has gone by when we hang up. Claudio Rafael, sitting on the couch, stares at the wall in front of him. Seated at the table, Ana Maria can’t believe it. “So that’s what it was… And if you hadn’t called, our file would still be in the same department with nobody looking after it… I don’t know how we’re going to manage in the meantime,” she says, holding her head.
Pour l’heure, leur demande d’asile, prés: For now, their asylum claim, filed at Toronto’s airport in April 2024, is still being processed, and they are waiting for the date of their tribunal hearing. A hearing that is crucial to their future, at which they will have to prove they were victims of persecution in their country of origin.
<strong>Discrimination, agressions, ségr: Discrimination, assaults, segregation – the violent daily reality of Roma in Romania
« En Roumanie, notre communauté est vict: “In Romania, our community is the target of so many prejudices and so much racism. When you’re Roma, you can’t find work, you can’t find housing outside the village, children are harassed and assaulted at school… That’s why my brother left for Canada, and that’s why we’re here today,” says Claudio Rafael Firu. The Roma community makes up nearly 9% of Romania’s population. Yet it faces one of the highest rates of social rejection among all groups vulnerable to discrimination, the Romanian Institute for Human Rights confirmed in 2021.
Certaines écoles vont jusqu’à mettre en: Some schools go as far as practising school segregation, separating classes according to students’ ethnic origin and place of residence, or designating “special” schools for Roma children. In 2021 in Romania, 51% of Roma children attended segregated schools, up from 28% in 2016, according to <l1>a study</l1> published in 2024 by the Council of Europe.
Amnistie internationale dénonçait égalem: Amnesty International also denounced hate speech against the Roma, including from political figures, in 2021. And the situation has not improved in recent years. In its <l1>2023-2024 report on Romania</l1>, the NGO recalls several serious incidents, including the torture of two Roma men by police officers in Tulcea, and the refusal of the Urziceni hospital to treat a pregnant Roma woman, who had to give birth on the sidewalk.
Pour le couple Firu, qui a vécu cette pe: For the Firu couple, who have lived through this persecution and know its repercussions, it is hard to understand why Canada would not recognize their suffering.
<strong>Une méconnaissance de l’histoire: A lack of knowledge of Roma history
« La migration forcée des Roms vers des: “The forced migration of Roma to countries like Canada is often misunderstood… They migrate because their rights are not respected and they are victims of discrimination every day,” explains Izabela Tiberiade, a human rights researcher. From Craiova, Romania, the city the Iordaches and the Firus come from, she shares her analysis of the complex situation of Roma seeking refuge in Canada, a country many of them see as a welcoming land.
Selon M<sup>me</sup> Tiberiade, plusieur: According to M<sup>s</sup>. Tiberiade, several institutional and cultural obstacles hinder Roma access to refugee status, despite Canada’s past efforts to open the door a little wider to this population and allow it to obtain asylum: “Even though Roma have Romanian passports, their ethnicity must be taken into account when processing their asylum claims.”
L’histoire de ce peuple hétérogène est e: The history of this heterogeneous people has indeed been marked by migration and persecution since its arrival in Europe in the 14<sup>th</sup> century. “The Nazi genocide marks a break in the recent history of the Roma. It represents the culmination of a centuries-old attitude of discrimination, stigmatization and persecution,” states the <l1>Roma Children Education Project</l1>.
« Aujourd’hui, le Canada les voit comme: “Today, Canada sees them as Romanian citizens of a so-called democratic country and doesn’t understand that they carry a whole history of intergenerational trauma,” Izabela Tiberiade says. “There is a direct connection with the <l1>Transnistria deportations</l1>, which refers to the Holocaust and Romanian Roma, because that is where the wave of migration to Canada began.” M<sup>s</sup>. Tiberiade, whose own uncle is a camp survivor, points to the lack of recognition of her community’s status as victims. “The Roma received no reparations policy or healing process” after the end of the Second World War.
Un manque qui serait l’un des facteurs à: That lack is said to be one of the factors behind the problems Roma face in Canada, but not the only one. The integration of Eastern European countries into the European Union (EU) in the 2000s marked a turning point. In 2004, Hungary, home to many Roma, joined the EU, followed by Romania and Bulgaria in 2007, and finally Croatia in 2013.
Cela permet aux habitants de ces pays, d: This exempted residents of those countries, now EU citizens, from visa requirements and triggered an exodus of Roma to Canada from 2007 to 2011. Faced with this new migration flow, the Conservative government of the day brought in the law stemming from Bill C-31.
<strong>C-31, campagnes publicitaires di: C-31, deterrent ad campaigns, prejudice: the impact of federal policies
Gina Csanyi-Robah, directrice et fondatr: Gina Csanyi-Robah, director and founder of the Canadian Romani Alliance and a teacher with the Vancouver School Board, has dedicated her life to raising awareness among the Canadian public of the challenges Roma face, particularly those seeking refuge in the country. In her view, Roma run up against institutional barriers that are the result of racial prejudice and deeply rooted discrimination in the asylum system.
L’un des moments marquants de cette inst: One of the defining moments in the institutionalization of discrimination against the Roma community came in 2012, when Stephen Harper’s Conservative government passed Bill C-31, titled the Protecting Canada’s Immigration System Act. “The government used terms like ‘fake refugees,’ implying that Roma were fleeing fictitious conditions, which created a climate of mistrust and rejection,” says the woman who was then director of the Toronto Roma Community Centre.
Le projet de loi C-31 instaure une série: Bill C-31 introduced a series of major changes, including a list of countries deemed “safe,” on which Romania appears. Asylum seekers from one of these “safe” countries face shorter deadlines to submit their claims, no right to appeal if they are refused, and restricted access to the pre-removal risk assessment (PRRA). “This law very clearly targeted the Roma community. As a result, acceptance rates for Roma refugee claims dropped sharply, staying at zero for several months after the law was passed,” says Gina Csanyi-Robah.
En 2013, Ottawa a été jusqu’à dépenser d: In 2013, Ottawa even went as far as spending public money on an advertising campaign, with large billboards, newspaper ads and radio spots in the Hungarian city of Miskolc. The goal? To discourage potential Roma asylum seekers from coming to Canada.
« Avis du gouvernement du Canada. Pour p: “Notice from the Government of Canada. To prevent abuse, Canada’s asylum system has changed. Those arriving with unfounded asylum claims will be sent home faster,” read the billboards in Miskolc, Hungary, in 2013. Photo: Facebook screenshot.
À l’époque, Amnistie internationale, l’A: At the time, Amnesty International, the Canadian Association of Refugee Lawyers, the Canadian Civil Liberties Association and the Canadian Council for Refugees decided to respond by forming the Justice for Immigrants and Refugees coalition. It denounced the regulation as “unconstitutional,” and criticized the fact that the list of “safe countries” was determined by the Immigration Minister without relying on expert advice, and called for its withdrawal.
Ce n’est qu’en 2019 que cette loi est fi: It was not until 2019 that the law was finally repealed. But it left scars. In September 2024, Harvard University, in collaboration with the Canadian Romani Alliance, published <l1>a report</l1> concluding that the vast majority of Roma Canadians had experienced discrimination because of their origins.
L’année dernière, la <l1>Commission de l: Last year, the <l1>Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada</l1> accepted 71% of the 203 Romanian asylum claims it processed (who were presumed to be mostly Roma). As a reminder, this protected status is granted if a person proves there is a risk of being tortured, having their life threatened, or being subjected to cruel and unusual treatment or punishment if they return to their country of origin.
On constate toutefois une persistance de: However, biases persist in judges’ decisions, which the expert attributes to the ignorance and lack of understanding surrounding the Roma community. Csanyi-Robah, whose Roma grandparents fled Hungary in 1956, points to the wide variation in asylum acceptance rates depending on the commissioner handling the case. “Take Romania, where the Iordaches are from: some judges reach a 100% acceptance rate, while others recognize only 37% of cases. What justifies such a gap?” asks <sup></sup>Csanyi-Robah.
« Les juges qui examinent les demandes d: “The judges who examine asylum claims still have unconscious prejudices against Roma. People who don’t know our community are often influenced by the negative stereotypes spread in the media or in Europe, where you sometimes see Roma living in poverty and begging in tourist areas,” says <sup></sup>Csanyi-Robah.
Alors que la campagne électorale fédéral: With the federal election campaign in full swing, she cites the attitude of political and judicial decision-makers as the key to a better future for Roma in Canada. The activist advocates cultural and historical training for Immigration commissioners. The Refugee Law Lab, for its part, recommends putting mechanisms in place to monitor commissioners’ work.
Par ailleurs, Claudio Rafael Firu a refu: Meanwhile, Claudio Rafael Firu refused the assistance of an interpreter during his interview with Immigration: “They’re Romanians, and I don’t trust the way they translate. I prefer to speak in French, even if it’s not perfect.” A fear that may be well founded, according to the researcher’s findings.
« J’ai eu un accès inédit à des transcri: “I had unprecedented access to transcripts of interviews with Roma asylum seekers who were assisted by an interpreter. What we see is that the interpreter doesn’t translate the asylum seekers’ words faithfully and gives their own opinion, saying, for example, that they don’t think what the person is saying is true,” the expert reveals. This language issue is all the more damaging because Roma already struggle to explain what they experience in Romania or elsewhere, adds Izabela Tiberiade.
Ana Maria Firu confie également se senti: Ana Maria Firu also says she feels lost and doesn’t know who to turn to for help with their application. “Canada doesn’t allow Roma to get specialized help with their administrative procedures. They often don’t know the asylum systems well and have a limited command of the language, so they end up facing language and institutional barriers,” says <sup></sup>Tiberiade.
Pendant des années, des organismes comme: For years, organizations such as Romanipe and the Toronto Roma Community Centre (TRCC) supported Roma asylum seekers and offered them front-line resources. But for lack of funding, this assistance could not be sustained. Today, Romanipe is no longer active, and the TRCC no longer offers direct services to asylum seekers. With no structured, organized community to rely on, newcomers turn to professionals who are sometimes unscrupulous.
Certains demandeurs d’asile roms rapport: Some Roma asylum seekers report having been treated in a discriminatory way by non-Roma lawyers of Eastern European origin. In 2017, the Toronto Star revealed that three Toronto lawyers of Hungarian origin – Viktor Hohots, Joseph Farkas and Erzsebet Jaszi – had been found guilty of gross professional misconduct in handling thousands of Roma refugee cases. The decision followed class actions filed by former clients and highlighted the systemic flaws of the asylum system.
Privés d’une représentation compétente,: Deprived of competent representation, these asylum seekers never truly had the chance to tell their stories and present their claims under fair conditions.
Pour améliorer la situation, Izabela Tib: To improve the situation, Izabela Tiberiade argues that the Canadian government should recognize the unique situation of Roma, and she is asking Ottawa to adopt asylum policies that take into account Roma history and particular needs. “Canada should have a real conversation with Romania at a diplomatic level, with professionals and with Roma who work for Roma,” she suggests.
Selon la spécialiste, il s’agit d’une co: According to the specialist, this is a sine qua non for fighting the discrimination Roma face in Canada and ensuring their genuine integration. For Tiberiade, there is no doubt that without concrete efforts to close these gaps, Roma will continue to face insurmountable challenges in their quest for safety and dignity in Canada.
Malgré ces défis, Gina Csanyi-Robah veut: Despite these challenges, Gina Csanyi-Robah wants to keep hope. She points out that progress is possible, such as the Canadian government’s official recognition of the Roma genocide during the Second World War: “That helped change perceptions and pave the way for more support for Roma,” she concludes.
De leur côté, Rafael Claudio et Ana Mari: For their part, Rafael Claudio and Ana Maria Firu want to believe that the country they hold responsible for the death of their loved ones will not subject their family to a new trauma and will allow them to begin a new chapter of their lives here.
<strong>Plusieurs membres présumés d’un: Several alleged members of a smuggling ring face prosecution in the United States
En mars, deux résidents d’Akwesasne, Ste: In March, two Akwesasne residents, Stephanie Square and Rahsontanohstha Delormier, were taken into custody pending extradition to the United States. They are accused of taking part in a smuggling ring operating on Mohawk territory, which straddles Quebec, Ontario and New York State.
Selon les autorités, M<sup>me</sup> Squa: According to the authorities, <sup></sup>Square allegedly bought a small boat used for illegal crossings, including the one on March 29, 2023, which cost the lives of eight people, including the Iordache family. That night, weather conditions were extremely dangerous. “They asked my brother for $24,000. They’re murderers, they knew it was risky,” says Claudio Rafael Firu.
Aux États-Unis, trois autres personnes o: In the United States, three other people have pleaded guilty in the case, including an American and two Akwesasne residents. They face serious charges, including alien smuggling resulting in death, and could be sentenced to life in prison.
